questions.question: Loose belts in an engine compartment will:

options.text: Fail to turn the water pump and/or fan properly, causing the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan run too much, causing the engine to run too cold.
Last longer than tight belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to turn the water pump and/or fan properly, causing the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts regularly. Loose belts will not turn the water pump and/or fan properly. This can cause your engine to overheat.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, opening the bus door:

options.text: Can help you hear an approaching train.
Should never be done.
Lets other noise in, making it harder to hear approaching trains.
Takes too long and is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you hear an approaching train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, you may open the bus door if it helps you see or hear an approaching train.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a vehicle as set by the manufacturer.
The total weight of the vehicle without any cargo.
The weight of cargo minus the containers used to transport it.
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a vehicle as set by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight of a vehicle as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic laws.
Complete the test without any traffic violations.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other vehicles are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other vehicles are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road driving test. You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals at all times, obey all traffic laws, and avoid any accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: How should you test your hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the brake pedal and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, you may have a leak.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Stay in the driver's lane.
Race the driver.
Ignore the driver's gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver's gestures.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Avoid eye contact, do not race them, and do not react to any angry gestures.

questions.question: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance will become ____ times longer.

options.text: Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance becomes four times longer. The force of a collision would also multiply by four.

questions.question: Stopping distance is affected by:

options.text: Speed.
Temperature.
Time of day.
Traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your speed. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of a vehicle's leaf spring leaves are missing during inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle will be taken out of service until it is fixed.
The vehicle is safe to drive since most of the spring is intact.
The driver will be asked to reduce the cargo weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will be taken out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle will be taken out of service until it is repaired.

questions.question: All cargo must be secured by at least ____ tie-down(s), regardless of size.

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured by at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. However, use at least two tie-downs no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect your braking distance?

options.text: It stays about the same.
It increases slightly.
It doubles.
It quadruples.

questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance increases by four times. Higher speeds require much longer distances to stop.

questions.question: When does front wheel braking work?

options.text: Only on packed snow.
Under all conditions.
Only if the road is dry.
Under most conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions, including ice and wet surfaces. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: What should you know if you see lights ahead while driving in fog?

options.text: You can assume the lights are on the road.
It may be a reflection.
It may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, you cannot rely on lights to show you where the road is. A vehicle with lights may have pulled off the road.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: Crossings controlled by flashing lights.
Crossings with no traffic control devices.
Crossings with gates that lower when trains approach.
Crossings that should never be crossed by a commercial vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) mean?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo.
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo is added.
The total weight of cargo only.
The maximum weight allowed to be transported.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus all its cargo.

questions.question: When does antifreeze help keep an engine working properly?

options.text: Only in cold weather.
Only in hot weather.
All year round.
While reducing fuel use.

questions.correctAnswerText: All year round.
questions.explanation: Keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system all year. Antifreeze helps your engine work well in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines during an inspection, which should NOT be true?

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: Listen for leaks in air hoses during your inspection. Make sure air hoses and electrical lines are not cut, worn, or damaged. Check that they are not twisted, pinched, or dragging against the tractor.

questions.question: What must you do before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?

options.text: It will have air pressure even when not running.
It will keep some air pressure when not running.
You must run it to build air pressure for the brakes to work.
It will keep air pressure when shut off for less than four hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must run it to build air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build pressure of at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in S-cam brakes, air pressure moves the:

options.text: Slack adjuster.
Axle.
Brake drum.
Alcohol evaporator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slack adjuster.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should the driver do?

options.text: Ignore the report and find issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Review the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, review the last inspection report if one exists. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed on the report.
